newsitem.title: JAMAICA: Rains end Jamaica drought, one death feared.
newsitem.headline: Rains end Jamaica drought, one death feared.

text.p: Jamaica remained under a severe weather alert Thursday after torrential rains ended the island's worst drought in 70 years.
The rains were blamed for the disappearance of at least one person.
Police said 15-year-old Paul Douglas was believed drowned after he attempted to ford a river in central Jamaica on Wednesday afternoon with two other people.
All three were swept away by the rushing waters, but Douglas' two companions were rescued by passers-by. Douglas' body had not been recovered by Thursday.

The rains ended a drought -- Jamaica's worst since 1927 -- during which parts of Kingston, the capital, were rationed to six hours of water per day for several weeks as water levels in reservoirs dropped to critically low levels.
The shortages were even more acute in rural areas that lack running water, as rivers and streams dried up.
